definition: The money moving in and out of a business over a period of time.
business_context_example: The company is profitable on paper, but cash flow is tight until clients pay.

definition: To reach the point where income equals costs, with no profit and no loss.
business_context_example: We break even at 25 students per course; everything above that is profit.

definition: The percentage of revenue left after costs are paid.
business_context_example: Group courses have a better profit margin than private lessons.

definition: The total money a business earns before any costs are taken out.
business_context_example: Revenue grew 20%, but so did our costs, so profit stayed flat.

definition: The total sales of a business in a period; also, how often staff leave and are replaced.
business_context_example: Annual turnover passed 500,000 euro for the first time.

definition: The regular costs of running a business, like rent, salaries and utilities.
business_context_example: Moving to a smaller office cut our overheads by a third.

definition: Costs that stay the same no matter how much you sell.
business_context_example: Rent and insurance are fixed costs, so a quiet month still hurts.

definition: Costs that go up or down depending on how much you produce or sell.
business_context_example: Printing course books is a variable cost: more students, more books.

definition: The final profit or loss figure at the end of a financial report.
business_context_example: Cutting the ad budget helped the bottom line but hurt new sign-ups.

definition: Making a profit.
business_context_example: After 18 months, the school is finally in the black.

definition: Losing money or having a negative balance.
business_context_example: January and February are always in the red for us.

definition: To accept that money owed will never be paid, and remove it from the accounts.
business_context_example: We had to write off 2,000 euro when the client's company closed.

definition: A financial statement showing what a company owns and owes at one moment.
business_context_example: The bank asked for our balance sheet before approving the loan.

definition: A report showing revenue, costs and profit over a period.
business_context_example: The income statement shows where the extra 8,000 euro of costs came from.

definition: Money that customers owe the business but haven't paid yet.
business_context_example: Accounts receivable is 15,000 euro, and half of it is over 60 days late.

definition: Money the business owes to its suppliers.
business_context_example: Accounts payable is due on the 15th, so keep that cash aside.

definition: A document requesting payment for goods or services.
business_context_example: I'll send the invoice today with 14-day payment terms.

definition: The agreed rules about when and how a customer must pay.
business_context_example: Our payment terms are 50% upfront, 50% on delivery.

definition: Not paid by the agreed date.
business_context_example: Three invoices are overdue, so I'm calling them this morning.

definition: To contact a customer repeatedly to get them to pay.
business_context_example: I spend an hour every Friday chasing invoices.

definition: Money paid before the work starts.
business_context_example: We ask for a 30% upfront payment from new corporate clients.

definition: A part payment made in advance to secure a booking or order.
business_context_example: The deposit is non-refundable if they cancel in the last week.

definition: Money given back to a customer.
business_context_example: She missed 4 lessons, so we agreed on a partial refund.

definition: A stated price for a job, given before the work begins.
business_context_example: I'll send a quote for the 12-week programme by Wednesday.

definition: A plan for how much money will be earned and spent.
business_context_example: The training budget for next year is 6,000 euro per department.

definition: Costing more than was planned.
business_context_example: The website came in 40% over budget because of the extra pages.

definition: To reduce spending.
business_context_example: We cut costs by dropping two software tools nobody used.

definition: To spend less because money is short.
business_context_example: Sales dropped in July, so we're tightening the belt until autumn.

definition: To do the calculations to check whether something makes financial sense.
business_context_example: Run the numbers before you promise that discount.

definition: A rough estimate, not an exact number.
business_context_example: Give me a ballpark figure and I'll tell you if it's realistic.

definition: A product or service that reliably brings in a lot of money.
business_context_example: Corporate courses are our cash cow; the app is still an experiment.

definition: How much you gain compared to what you spent.
business_context_example: The return on investment from the trade fair was poor: one client.

definition: The exact level of sales where you stop losing money.
business_context_example: Our break-even point drops if we teach online instead of renting rooms.

definition: The money available for day-to-day running of the business.
business_context_example: We need more working capital to pay teachers before clients pay us.

definition: Money borrowed that must be paid back, usually with interest.
business_context_example: The bank offered a loan at 6% over 5 years.

definition: The percentage charged for borrowing money.
business_context_example: If the interest rate rises again, we'll postpone the second office.

definition: Money that is owed.
business_context_example: The company is growing but carrying too much debt.

definition: The value of ownership in a company after debts are subtracted.
business_context_example: He put in 50,000 euro for a 20% equity stake.

definition: A person or company that owns part of a business.
business_context_example: Shareholders meet twice a year to approve the accounts.

definition: A share of profit paid out to owners.
business_context_example: The board decided to reinvest instead of paying a dividend.

definition: A prediction of future sales, costs or profit.
business_context_example: Our forecast for Q4 assumes two new corporate contracts.

definition: A three-month period used for financial reporting.
business_context_example: We'll review the numbers at the end of the quarter.

definition: The 12-month period a company uses for accounting.
business_context_example: Our fiscal year ends on 31 December, same as the calendar year.

definition: Compared with the same period last year.
business_context_example: Enrolments are up 12% year on year.

definition: An official check of a company's financial records.
business_context_example: The audit found two invoices recorded in the wrong month.

definition: Value Added Tax, a tax added to the price of goods and services.
business_context_example: The price is 1,200 euro plus VAT.

definition: A form declaring income and tax owed to the authorities.
business_context_example: The accountant files our tax return in March.

definition: An expense that can be subtracted from income before tax is calculated.
business_context_example: Professional training is tax-deductible for most companies.

definition: A request to be paid back for money spent on work.
business_context_example: Submit your travel expense claim with the receipts by Friday.

definition: The list of employees and the wages the company pays them.
business_context_example: Payroll runs on the 25th of each month.

definition: To persuade someone to accept a lower price.
business_context_example: They tried to bargain us down by 20%, and we met in the middle.
